attempted_claim: Let d>=3 and 0<alpha<d-1. Let P^{d-1}={(x,|x|^2):x in [0,1]^{d-1}} in R^d. Does there exist a Borel probability measure nu supported on a subset of P^{d-1} such that: (i) dim_H supp nu = alpha; (ii) for every epsilon>0, nu(B(x,r)) <<_{alpha,epsilon} r^{alpha-epsilon} for all x, r>0; (iii) for every epsilon>0, |hat{nu}(xi)| <<_{alpha,epsilon} (1+|xi|)^{-alpha/2+epsilon} for all xi; (iv) for every p>2(d+1)/alpha, ||hat{f dnu}||_{L^p(R^d)} <<_p ||f||_{L^2(nu)} for all f in L^2(nu)? Strict inequality p>2(d+1)/alpha only; no endpoint, exact Ahlfors-regularity, or exact Fourier decay claimed.
decisive_failure: The investigation established sharpness and a structural gap but no construction: closing the 2(d-1-alpha)/alpha exponent gap requires a new sharp fractal restriction theorem for singular measures on the paraboloid plus curved-phase normal-direction decay, both beyond the reach of bounded computation in this pass. The exponent-gap script is verification of the obstruction, not evidence for existence.
